name: Lesotho
summary: Lesotho taxes residents on worldwide income at 20% and 30%. Gains on investment assets, including foreign securities, are taxed as ordinary income at up to 30%, and foreign dividends are taxable at up to 30% with a foreign tax credit; dividends from Lesotho companies are excluded from residents' income. There is no wealth, estate, inheritance or gift tax. The exemption for foreign investment income in the Income Tax Act applies only to expatriates working under technical services contracts, not to a passive investor family.

regimes.name: Lesotho tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide income tax at 20%/30%, capital gains included; no estate, gift or wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if having a normal place of abode in Lesotho and present at any time in the year, present more than 182 days in any 12-month period, or resident under ordinary common-law tests. Non-citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on the disposal of investment assets (shares, securities, investment property) are property income, included in chargeable income and taxed at the normal rates (20% / 30%). Residents are taxed on worldwide income, so gains on foreign securities are taxable, with a foreign tax credit for foreign tax. Gains on personal-use assets are excluded.

sources.title: EY Worldwide Personal Tax and Immigration Guide 2025-26 (March 2026 edition)
Guide on Taxation of Employment Income 2026-27

capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: 2026/27 rates: 20% on chargeable income up to M 6,480 a month (M 77,760 a year), 30% above; non-refundable credit M 1,020 a month.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Income Tax Act 1993 s. 20 (property income includes gains on the disposal of investment assets) and s. 62 (losses on investment assets only against such gains). Section 24 exempts foreign-source property income and gains on assets generating foreign-source income only for an 'expatriate taxpayer', defined as a non-citizen resident employed or engaged under a technical services contract; a passive investor family does not qualify. EY's summary states the expatriate exemption without that condition.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 30% top marginal rate applied to the full gain on any investment asset, domestic or foreign; no holding period relief. Cost-base indexation was not checked.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading gains are business income at the same 30% top rate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide basis for residents (s. 103 per RSL practice note); foreign tax credit for foreign tax on foreign-source income.
open_questions: Whether the cost base of investment assets is indexed for inflation was not checked.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by a Lesotho resident company are not included in a resident shareholder's gross income (Income Tax Act s. 87(6)); the company has already paid tax. Foreign dividends are property income of a resident and are taxed at up to 30%, with a foreign tax credit.

sources.title: EY Worldwide Personal Tax and Immigration Guide 2025-26 (March 2026 edition)
Practice note: Taxation of Foreign Nationals

dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Domestic dividends: excluded from residents' gross income. 25% WHT applies only to Lesotho-source dividends paid to non-residents (s. 107).
dividends.important_exceptions: EY states that resident individuals are not subject to tax on dividends without distinguishing domestic and foreign dividends; the Act's exclusion in s. 87(6) covers dividends paid by resident companies only, so foreign dividends are scored as taxable. The s. 24 exemption for foreign property income applies only to expatriate taxpayers under technical services contracts.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic 0 (s. 87(6)). Foreign: 30% top rate on the gross dividend, before credit for foreign tax borne.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 25% on dividends paid to non-residents (exempt if paid out of concessionally taxed manufacturing income), reducible by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: Very small: Botswana, Eswatini, Mauritius, South Africa, United Kingdom; TIEAs with Guernsey and Isle of Man (EY 2026). No US treaty.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 25% CIT (10% manufacturing). Not modelled.
open_questions: Foreign dividends of resident individuals scored as taxable at 30% based on the Act's worldwide scope; EY's wording ('not subject to tax on dividends') could suggest otherwise. Confirm with RSL.

sources.title: EY Worldwide Personal Tax and Immigration Guide 2025-26 (March 2026 edition)

inheritance.summary: No estate, inheritance or gift tax (EY 2026).

sources.title: EY Worldwide Personal Tax and Immigration Guide 2025-26 (March 2026 edition)

inheritance.important_exceptions: Transfer (stamp/registration) costs on Lesotho land and whether a transfer by gift is a disposal at market value for income tax were not checked.
open_questions: Whether a gift or a transfer on death is treated as a disposal at market value for income tax on investment-asset gains was not checked.

residency.tax_residency_test: Income Tax Act s. 5(1): an individual is resident if (a) they have a normal place of abode in Lesotho and are present for part of the year, (b) present more than 182 days in any consecutive 12 months, (c) a Lesotho government official abroad, or (d) otherwise resident under ordinary tests (presence, ties, home). Tax year 1 April to 31 March.

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: Non-citizens need a residence permit from the Department of Immigration; no residence-by-investment programme was identified (not researched).

sources.title: Practice note: Taxation of Foreign Nationals
EY Worldwide Personal Tax and Immigration Guide 2025-26 (March 2026 edition)

corporate.summary: 25% CIT; 10% for manufacturing income (and exports outside SACU); capital gains taxed as ordinary income. Dividends paid to resident shareholders are excluded from their income; 25% WHT on dividends to non-residents.

sources.title: EY Worldwide Corporate Tax Guide 2025 (October 2025 edition)

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed. Lesotho's 30% on foreign dividends and gains is above US long-term rates, so the Lesotho tax would usually be the binding layer. No US-Lesotho income tax treaty.
open_questions: The consolidated Income Tax Act on the RSL site runs only to 1 April 2012; later amendments (other than the 2026/27 rates in the RSL employment guide) were not checked.
